$comment: Every user-visible capability, and what actually proves it works.
The distinction this file exists to keep honest: a SHELL journey proves the application starts
and configures itself; a WORKFLOW journey proves a customer got what they came for. Only the
second kind counts as a feature being verified. Unit tests and mock-call assertions never do.
status: green (passing real-binary proof), red (a real-binary journey is written and failing),
unproven (the customer capability exists but has no product-level success proof), planned
(the named non-overlapping journey is not written yet), or covered-indirectly.
A red entry is not a gap in coverage -- it is coverage that has found something. Source tests
and screenshots of a surface alone never promote a customer outcome to green.

binary.e2e: npm run build:e2e-binary publishes the guarded nonshipping E2E application into the managed external cache; every launch holds the apps/e2e cache lease while re-verifying receipts/current.json, its immutable manifest, exact inventory and every file digest, with no repository-target fallback
binary.installed: NSIS setup from --features production, exercised by the isolated installed smoke

$comment: What the source-level suite proves after the 2026-08-20 deletion was independently audited and reversed.
A test double is not product-level proof, but that does not make every doubled test worthless.
The deleted suites contain hostile accessor, malformed-event, cancellation, stale-owner,
exact-once cleanup, protocol and persistence checks that are difficult and expensive to
exercise exhaustively through a GUI. They are restored as fast behavioral contract coverage.
Real-binary journeys remain the authority for whether a customer capability works. Source-level
tests complement those journeys; they do not replace them. The restored suite is green after
updating two stale preview fixtures to the real transport-index contract.

restored.reason: behavioral contract and adversarial coverage remains valuable even when a boundary is doubled
restored.productProof: none; capability claims require a real-binary journey

$comment: There are no synthetic media fixtures. Customer acquisition is proven independently against
a real YouTube URL. Deterministic cancellation and A-to-B identity use two pinned real videos
behind an exact, throttled loopback capability compiled only into the hidden E2E graph.
The colour-bars clips that used to live in e2e/fixtures/media proved the decoder could open a
file this repository had generated, which is not a claim about anything a customer plays.
media.why: First video published to YouTube. Nineteen seconds, no music licence, the least likely link on the platform to be deleted or region-locked.
media.cachedAt: managed external cache assets/e2e/real-media (input-only; copied into each disposable run root; the old repository target is read-only rollback input)
media.enginePackagesCachedAt: managed external cache assets/e2e/engine-packages (package bytes only; every journey still has a fresh database, projects, WebView and logs)

$comment: Everything the harness replaces, and nothing else. Each one is a native dialog a WebDriver
session cannot drive; each is compiled only into the e2e-automation channel; each is bounded
to a reviewed directory; and each hands its answer to exactly the same code a person's click
reaches, so every product invariant after that point is the real one.
Nothing else is substituted. No IPC is mocked, no capability flag is fabricated, no database
row is written behind the interface, no private helper is invoked.

saveDialog.boundedBy: OSG_E2E_FIXTURE_ROOT; must be an existing directory; the file it resolves to must not already exist
saveDialog.replaces: every native save dialog through dialog_paths.rs
saveDialog.handsTo: the requested media, narration, subtitle, archive, or image exporter, which writes the real bytes
saveDialog.note: A DIRECTORY, not a file path: only the application knows the proposed file name. In an e2e-automation build, missing, invalid, out-of-root, or occupied staging is a typed refusal. Native picker/save implementations are compiled only outside that feature, so an autonomous journey cannot fall back to File Explorer.

downloadOrigin.boundedBy: an exact two-URL allow-list fixed before launch; canonical http://127.0.0.1 unprivileged ports; one 256-bit token per MP4 URL
downloadOrigin.replaces: only the remote origin for cancellation timing; yt-dlp inspection, native job registration, streaming, cancellation, candidate claim and activation remain the product path
downloadOrigin.productionProof: the ordinary validator rejects the same loopback URLs even in an automation-capable build, and the separate constructor is absent unless osg-download/e2e-automation is propagated from the desktop E2E feature
downloadOrigin.independentNetworkProof: urlToPreview remains the real YouTube/yt-dlp smoke and does not use this origin

dataRoot.why: SHGetKnownFolderPath ignores %LOCALAPPDATA%, so a run cannot be isolated from outside the process

screenshotEvidence.root: managed external cache evidence/<workflow>/ (the runner holds the dedicated evidence lease from attempt creation through finalization, then releases and post-prunes)
screenshotEvidence.index: Each workflow folder keeps the three newest immutable attempts plus its latest successful proof, an ordered README index, and an atomic latest-success.json pointer. Every retained attempt contains its own screenshots, independent artifacts, diagnostics and manifest.
screenshotEvidence.windowMode: The e2e-automation binary runs as a full-size real WebView whose complete native rectangle is derived beyond the union of every attached monitor and excluded from the taskbar. The HWND is made non-focusable (WS_EX_NOACTIVATE through Tauri's safe API), and repositioning uses SWP_NOACTIVATE. The embedded driver may keep it compositor-visible so GPU/video work advances; every journey rejects an interactive-desktop coordinate in its own test path, and no journey uses Windows computer-control or a native dialog. Playback/render journeys prove frame and media progress directly; visibility is never used as a proxy.
screenshotEvidence.interaction: Embedded WebDriver protocol only: no SendInput, physical cursor movement, focus stealing, or native picker/save implementation.
screenshotEvidence.authority: Screenshots expose customer-visible truth and aesthetic defects; files, SQLite, logs, hashes, ffprobe, decoded pixels, and second-process restoration remain the independent success oracles.
screenshotEvidence.provenance: Every attempt records the source commit and dirty paths plus the exact E2E executable path, byte size and SHA-256. The three newest attempts and latest successful proof are retained; only a completed passing attempt may atomically replace latest-success.json, so a red rerun cannot erase prior green proof. Retention is inventory-validated, journaled and recoverable after a partial quarantine.

journeys.name: urlToPreview
journeys.capability: A customer pastes a real YouTube link and saves the video to their disk.
chain: the application installs FFmpeg, yt-dlp and Deno from its reviewed delivery catalog
it resolves the real URL and names the real video
it scans the URL for the formats it actually offers
it downloads the chosen quality and writes the real bytes to the chosen destination

the quality scan returns real formats
a real file of non-trivial size appears at the staged destination
no error is visible

the file on disk
substitutes: the native save dialog, through OSG_E2E_MEDIA_DESTINATION
journeys.note: 'Download Only' is save-to-disk, not load-into-editor: it downloads, exports to the chosen path and discards the candidate. Measured green on the real binary: the scan returned 240p/144p and the export wrote 440,628 bytes.

journeys.name: urlLocalAsrPreview
journeys.capability: A real URL becomes one durable editor project whose acquired subtitles are drawn on the video.
chain: resolve a real YouTube URL
download it through the generation path rather than Download Only
activate exactly one durable subtitle project
use provider captions when supplied, otherwise transcribe with the real managed local ASR engine
publish cues and a canvas-atlas preview frame
assertions: the active URL does not change during media preparation
exactly one subtitle project owns the downloaded media
durable cues and canvas-composited pixels are both present
no inline video error or failure toast is visible
oracles: visible DOM and screenshot
the application's own SQLite database, read only
journeys.note: The first run reproduced the reported projectScopeMismatch: mounting the file tab reactivated downloaded media as a local upload while the renderer minted another asset-keyed project, leaving cues and media in separate projects. The unchanged real URL path is now green with exactly one project, six durable provider cues, a seek into a real cue, and a screenshot showing that cue in native preview pixels. If a provider supplies no track, the same journey continues through the managed local ASR engine.

journeys.name: downloadCancellationRetryIdentity
journeys.capability: A customer cancels a partial URL acquisition, retries immediately, then selects distinct URL B without stale A ever reappearing.
assertions: public cancellation aborts the active range transfer and immediate retry registers a distinct native operation and job
the cancelled job publishes no project, media, artifact, ownership edge, successful-job claim, alias or leftover scratch bytes
retry publishes exact source-A bytes with exact successful-job provenance
starting B withdraws every visible/session identity for A before B can finish
B becomes the sole active media while A remains a distinct durable historical project
every artifact-root file is reconciled to SQLite: two durable downloads and two waveform-cache entries, with no orphan or scratch bytes
oracles: public WebView controls and screenshot evidence
launcher-owned path-free range request ledger
SQLite read-only ownership and provenance queries
managed filesystem walk plus independent SHA-256 of both durable artifacts
complete SQLite-to-filesystem reconciliation for native waveform-cache artifacts
substitutes: the remote byte origin only, through the compile-time exact loopback capability described above
journeys.note: Green in off-screen real-binary attempt 20260825155018591-64168-fab31072 against automation binary af9691ba1b57f4055b15ec541a5407ff10e3563f2e66d79420308237647e9ff1. All five screenshots were inspected. The run proved an aborted partial A transfer, a distinct successful retry, exact source bytes, early A withdrawal during B, distinct durable A/B projects, and exact ownership of both download and waveform-cache artifacts.

journeys.name: failedDownloadNoStale
journeys.capability: When a replacement URL download fails after real inspection, the previously playing source is withdrawn honestly: one typed failure toast, history-only residue, and never resurrected or fabricated media.
oracles: a launcher-owned exact loopback origin whose path-free event ledger proves the real transfer shapes: source A fully ranged and played, source C inspected once then rejected with real HTTP 503
public WebView controls only, with a DOM stale-media sweep proving no visible or playable media survives the failure
read-only SQLite durability state proving source A remains solely historical and source C published nothing
four inspected screenshots under the managed external evidence lane/failed-download-no-stale
substitutes: the remote byte origin only, through the compile-time exact loopback capability
journeys.note: Green in off-screen real-binary attempt 20260826234117169-59440-d6f71134 (exe sha256 0b443bb8d34b7b82a9c0dad26b22049490efeae2a4700df33dd407cc460c7028). All four screenshots inspected. The origin ledger shows A's complete 4372373-byte ranged transfer, then C passing yt-dlp's real inspection before three genuine 503 rejections; the customer saw exactly one typed download-failure toast, no stale or fabricated media, and A surviving only as history.

import subtitles through the real drop target

relaunch the process
the project restores and the compositor publishes a frame again
oracles: visible DOM
the application's own SQLite database, read only
substitutes: the native open dialog, through OSG_E2E_MEDIA_SELECTION
journeys.note: The seed and verification phases now run in two separate WDIO invocations and therefore two separate desktop processes against one isolated profile. The former reloadSession-based test only replaced WebDriver's session while leaving the application alive and was not relaunch proof.

Arabic inside brackets, which used to be refused as a mirrored character

journeys.name: nativeToolsInstall
journeys.capability: A clean machine installs FFmpeg, yt-dlp and Deno from the reviewed catalog, verifying every digest.
oracles: the real Settings > Tools controls and row states
the native status boundary in a fresh desktop process
an independent filesystem walk, exact receipt comparison, size check and SHA-256 of every installed executable and notice
journeys.note: Starts without the persistent E2E tools junction, installs all three tools through customer controls, and verifies every installed byte against the static catalog or immutable dynamic yt-dlp delivery record. The coordinator then changes one byte of yt-dlp without changing its size, launches a new desktop process, requires a fail-closed corrupt/quarantined state, uses the visible Repair control, and revalidates the complete tree.

journeys.name: canvasPlaybackPerformance
journeys.capability: Continuous subtitle playback remains responsive and memory-bounded on real media.
oracles: the real video clock advances at least five seconds during a six-second sample
the persistent composition canvas publishes substantially more frames than the deleted 10 fps PNG transport
every presentation sample strictly inside an authored cue retains that cue on the main preview canvas
PerformanceObserver records no blocking task and the JavaScript heap does not grow without bound
an ordered screenshot and machine-readable sample are retained under the managed external evidence lane
journeys.note: The rebuilt real binary advanced 6.032 seconds during a 6.073-second sample, published 115 compositor frames and 603 animation frames from the real 15 fps video, retained the expected subtitle in all 495 active-cue samples, rebuilt the static overlay once, recorded zero long tasks, and grew the JavaScript heap by 4.09 MB. The visible canvas is now presentation-only: each revision arrives as one complete video-plus-subtitle paint from a back buffer.

journeys.name: nativeExportDecoded
journeys.capability: An exported video decodes to frames that match the preview at the same instants.
oracles: visible DOM and native render queue
the saved file on disk
independent ffprobe stream and duration inspection
independent FFmpeg decode and SSIM against the cropped canvas composition viewport
journeys.note: Green against the rebuilt real binary: native decode/composite/encode/mux completed, the saved MP4 contained independently probed video and audio streams with the expected duration, and its decoded Neon frame (Arial, border, glow, shadow and background) matched the persistent canvas preview at SSIM 0.973657. The journey found and drove four earlier product defects to green: missing subtitle admission, selecting a video track as audio plus malformed MP4 Opus parameters, refusing a valid audio-tail presentation after video EOS, and rejecting every successful publication because the artifact and immutable media snapshot were correctly separate files.

journeys.name: localFileImport
journeys.capability: A customer opens a video already on their disk.
oracles: ffprobe and SHA-256 of the staged source, read before the application ever sees the file
the app's reported duration/dimensions against the independent probe, plus the private native media-server URL shape
read-only SQLite media identity and the persisted windows-utf16le location pointer, decoded, contained to the owned artifact store, and re-hashed independently against the selected bytes
three screenshots under the managed external evidence lane/local-file-import
journeys.note: Green in off-screen real-binary attempt 20260827010107629-34704-9ec306f1 (exe sha256 f47148d4fee0…). All three screenshots inspected. Import is by owned copy: the persisted windows-utf16le location pointer decoded to a content-addressed file inside the isolated artifact store holding exactly the selected 440628 bytes (SHA-256 equal), the editor reported the probe-exact 19.014s duration and dimensions, streamed from the private native media server, showed the customer their file name, fabricated no cues, and decoded a real mid-file frame with a ready waveform. The first run corrected the journey itself: it assumed in-place references where the product correctly copies.

journeys.name: timelineBoundary
journeys.capability: Timeline boundaries agree, delete-all is durable, and a new transcription streams without resurrecting deleted cues.
chain: open real media through the guarded native file-selection boundary
import one ordinary cue and one ending exactly at the playable boundary
inspect actual waveform canvas pixels against the real video duration
select through the documented Ctrl+A shortcut and delete through the keyboard
start the real local ASR engine from the empty durable track
observe fresh visible cues while the overall generation operation is still active
wait separately for the same transcribe job to succeed
oracles: waveform canvas pixels before and after the calculated seekable boundary
the visible range action bar and cue list
the application's own SQLite cue count, read only
ordered screenshots under the managed external evidence lane/timeline-boundary
journeys.note: The journey owns two connected invariants. First, waveform, pointer selection and Ctrl+A share the real media boundary, no selectable range extends into subtitle-only or visual-gutter time, and deleting the selection drives SQLite to zero. Second, generation starts from that empty Rust checkpoint: deleted imported text may never reappear, a MutationObserver must witness newly transcribed rows while the overall generation operation is still active, and those rows must later be durable with a separately observed succeeded job state.

journeys.name: asrGeneration
journeys.capability: Subtitles are generated from the audio by a local ASR engine.
chain: open a real downloaded video through the real file control
verify/install and start Faster-Whisper Turbo from the reviewed managed package
select the full timeline through the documented Ctrl+A customer shortcut
extract audio through Media Foundation and transcribe it in the managed Python worker
publish cues into the editor, draw them through the persistent canvas, and persist them
oracles: visible cue text
the persistent composition canvas
the application's own SQLite jobs, cues and latest project revision, read only
journeys.note: The first real run exposed two production defects that mocks missed: package-status polling launched overlapping full-tree scans during publication, reaching 562 threads and about 11 GiB private memory; and Rust emitted job_id/timeline_offset_ms while JavaScript required jobId/timelineOffsetMs, so the first progress event cancelled every healthy job. Both are fixed and the unchanged journey is green.

journeys.name: multiWindowAsrGeneration
journeys.capability: The public maximum-duration setting splits one long video into exactly four native ASR jobs whose results stream monotonically, merge durably, and restore after relaunch without resurrecting deleted cues.
chain: stage a 204-second H.264/AAC video built offline from ten repetitions of the tracked real AMI meeting speech fixture
import and durably delete four uniquely named old cues through Ctrl+A and Delete
select the full media through Ctrl+A and set the real ASR maximum-duration slider to one minute
observe four contiguous ranges, four distinct native transcribe jobs, and one live timeline publication per range
compare the exact streamed cue union with SQLite's ordered durable track
start a second hidden desktop process and restore the same jobs, media, cues, and drawable native preview
oracles: the customer-facing slider value and visible four-part prediction
processing-ranges and streaming-update events observed without replacing their product consumers
monotonically growing visible timeline snapshots while aggregate processing is active
the application's own SQLite jobs and cues, read only
a second independently launched desktop process
six ordered screenshots under the managed external evidence lane/multi-window-asr-persistence
fixtures: the managed external assets/e2e/four-window-asr-media/asr-four-windows-real-speech.mp4 cache, generated offline by the reviewed native-tools FFmpeg and semantically probed before use
journeys.runsAgainst: two independent guarded e2e-binary processes sharing one isolated profile
journeys.note: Green on 2026-08-27 across both hidden desktop processes with all six screenshots inspected: four owned native jobs from the public one-minute setting, one live in-window publication per range while the aggregate stayed active, an 82-cue durable merge equal to the streamed union, and a second process restoring the exact track (the virtualized lyrics list is verified through the editor's own count surface plus viewport-prefix equality). Along the way this journey flushed out and drove fixes for the engine-status verification race, the Ctrl+A dead half-second, and the scenario's nested application-lease acquisition; one intermittent aggregate death remains recorded under knownProductFindings with a fail-fast capture armed.

knownProductFindings.finding: The built application navigated its main window to a file:// directory listing of the frontend path and the process died on the first IPC message.
knownProductFindings.note: The managed build contexts passed build.frontendDist as an absolute Windows path in TAURI_CONFIG. Tauri parses that as a URL whose scheme is the drive letter, so codegen embedded no assets and get_app_url navigated to the raw path, which WebView2 rendered as a file:// directory index; wry's WebMessageReceived handler then panicked unwrapping Request::uri on that URL, killing the process. The same override shape was wired into the production package lane. All producers now emit a validated relative directory through one shared tauriFrontendDistOverride helper, the build-context guard rejects the absolute form, and the release-readiness pin tracks the new shape.

knownProductFindings.finding: Every journey screenshot failed with an extension error before any evidence could be captured.
knownProductFindings.note: WebdriverIO 9 validates that saveScreenshot targets end in .png, while workflow evidence stages payloads under journal-owned .tmp names before their atomic rename. Capture and failure promotion now take the PNG bytes via takeScreenshot and stage them through the existing journaled write, leaving the recovery contract untouched.

knownProductFindings.finding: Every cache prune deleted every live lease, so concurrent managed commands could steal each other's lanes.
knownProductFindings.note: ConvertFrom-Json auto-converts the lease marker's ISO-8601 creation field into a DateTime; stringifying it dropped sub-second precision and the UTC suffix, so the tick comparison classified every live owner as a reused PID. A prune stole the running E2E build's lease mid-compile and its publication failed closed. The comparison now uses the DateTime directly, and a regression test proves a live-owner lease survives Prune and blocks a second acquire.

knownProductFindings.finding: The from-empty native-tools scenario could not start because the application's own store directory was misread as an attached cache, and a live run root's designed junction wedged every managed prune.
knownProductFindings.note: The application creates data/native-tools eagerly at boot and the WDIO worker re-runs the config after the launcher's service has spawned the binary, so the disabled-cache guard now refuses only links, not ordinary directories. Separately, the cache size walker failed closed on the engine-packages junction inside an actively leased staging run root; it now skips staging directory reparse points without following them while every other lane stays strict.

knownProductFindings.finding: A four-window local ASR aggregate intermittently stopped after the second window with the visible timeline wiped and no error surface.
knownProductFindings.note: Observed once on binary 813c5c18: two of four transcribe jobs existed (both succeeded natively), only window one ever published a streaming update, and the error path restored the pre-run baseline of zero rows, leaving an empty timeline with generation inactive, no toast captured, and no runtime or inline error. The window-two completion must have thrown between native success and the streaming publish (result mapping or delivery validation). The journey now fails fast at generation-death and captures the toast history in the same instant, so the next recurrence names the thrown error. Not reproduced across four later full runs.
knownProductFindings.recurrenceWatch: the seed phase's generation-death capture in journeys/multiWindowAsrPersistence.journey.js

knownProductFindings.finding: An application killed during an engine install could never boot again once its cache directory was cleared.
knownProductFindings.note: Persistent package stores under local data shared the cache-rooted staging authority, so the journal that owned an interrupted install's .staging entry lived in a directory the customer (or an E2E run-root teardown) can clear independently of the store. The orphaned entry then made recover_staging fail closed and the Tauri setup hook panicked before the window existed. Store managers now always prepare their staging authority inside the store root (the ui-fonts store already did), so the journal and the entry it owns can only be deleted together and boot-time reconciliation reclaims interrupted installs. A cancelled native export separately left its partial container behind because the unfinalized Media Foundation sink tears down asynchronously; discard now retries the delete within a bound.

knownProductFindings.finding: A successful URL download wrote the requested video and then showed a failure toast while leaving the modal open.
knownProductFindings.note: MediaExportEvent camel-cased its variant name but emitted bytes_written while the strict WebView boundary required bytesWritten. The completion acknowledgement was rejected after the file had already been written. The Rust producer now pins the exact field contract, and the journey re-inspects terminal UI after the file appears so bytes-on-disk cannot hide a visible failure.

knownProductFindings.finding: A freshly imported subtitle file was presented as saved but existed only in React memory.
knownProductFindings.note: The lyrics editor treated every incoming track as its saved baseline, which disabled Save. The import handler did not write the track, so a real process restart lost it. Desktop import now waits for an exact-project checkpoint, with project identity checks before and after the write, before publishing the rows to the editor.

knownProductFindings.finding: Persistence journeys described a WebDriver session replacement as an application relaunch.
knownProductFindings.note: The embedded Tauri service starts the application in onPrepare and stops it in onComplete; browser.reloadSession never restarts that process. Persistence scenarios now run seed and verification as separate WDIO invocations against one isolated profile. The stale helper and diagnostic were deleted.

knownProductFindings.finding: An autonomous narration export opened a real native save dialog when the harness expected staging.
knownProductFindings.note: Only media_export used the staging helper, and invalid staging fell back to the OS. All picker/save calls now cross one boundary whose automation implementation either returns a validated path inside the disposable fixture root or a typed refusal; the OS implementations are cfg-excluded. A source invariant rejects future bypasses.

knownProductFindings.finding: Aligned narration publication had no project ownership contract.
knownProductFindings.note: Alignment now requires every input artifact to be owned by the same existing project and publishes its result under that exact project and native job. Unowned and cross-project clips are rejected before work starts.

knownProductFindings.finding: Installing a speech engine cancelled itself when native progress did not advance its durable job sequence.
knownProductFindings.note: The speech package producer emitted a channel progress frame even when Job::set_progress returned an unchanged snapshot. The strict JavaScript ledger correctly treated the repeated sequence as replay. Native speech package progress now emits only after the durable sequence advances, matching the ASR package contract.

knownProductFindings.finding: Every generated narration artifact had project_id NULL.
knownProductFindings.note: Narration crossed IPC with only lifecycle and job ownership, so outputs could not be isolated, restored or cleaned by project. The exact subtitle-project alias is now captured before generation, revalidated after asynchronous setup, required as a UUIDv7 at both JavaScript boundaries, checked against SQLite before native job registration, and attached to every narration artifact publication.

knownProductFindings.finding: Every real local-ASR job was cancelled on its first progress event.
knownProductFindings.note: AsrJobEvent camel-cased enum variants but not struct fields. The real Rust Channel sent job_id/timeline_offset_ms; the JavaScript boundary correctly required jobId/timelineOffsetMs and cancelled the malformed channel. The Rust serializer now uses rename_all_fields and pins its exact wire shape in a producer-side test.

knownProductFindings.finding: Engine package status polling repeatedly verified a multi-gigabyte target while its install was still publishing.
knownProductFindings.note: A real run reached 562 desktop threads, roughly 11 GiB private memory and 55 GiB cumulative reads. Status now defers to the active operation, cold verification is single-flight, and verification holds a runtime lease against concurrent mutation. The next real run stayed near 57 threads and roughly 400 MiB during the same boundary.

knownProductFindings.finding: Native export was disabled even when imported subtitles were visible.
knownProductFindings.note: VideoRenderingSection omitted RenderSettingsRow.hasSubtitles. The real control now receives the actual project state and exposes a bounded admission diagnostic.

knownProductFindings.finding: The audio decoder selected a video track and could not interpret MP4 Opus dOps channel metadata.
knownProductFindings.note: Track selection now requires audio parameters, and exact mapping-family-0 dOps data is canonicalized to OpusHead with the correct layout. The committed H.264/AAC fixture and the real VP9/Opus download both decode.

knownProductFindings.finding: Videos whose audio presentation slightly outlasted the final video sample were refused as truncated.
knownProductFindings.note: At clean video EOS inside a positive declared presentation duration, decode holds the last actual video frame to the declared end. Targets at or beyond the duration and durationless truncation remain refusals.

knownProductFindings.finding: Every successful native render publication was rejected after the artifact had already succeeded.
knownProductFindings.note: Validation incorrectly required the rendered artifact and its immutable media snapshot to be the same filesystem object. It now verifies content identity, registers the already-verified handle, and commits success only after result creation is usable, with rollback cleanup.

knownProductFindings.finding: The native subtitle preview was refused at every playhead position except the very start.
knownProductFindings.note: The response validator required the frame URL's path index to equal the SCENE's frame index. They are different numbers: a preview publishes one image per capability, so the transport index is always 0, which `FrameLease::frame_url` states and does. The two agree only at frame 0, so the preview worked on a freshly opened project sitting at the start and was refused as soon as the timeline moved. It survived because every journey until now looked at the first frame.

knownProductFindings.finding: A preview response refused by the WebView reported one opaque code for eight different disagreements.
knownProductFindings.note: Naming each check is what turned nativePreviewRejected into previewResponseFrameIndex, which named the defect above.

knownProductFindings.finding: A preview refusal from inside the render left no trace in the application's own log.
knownProductFindings.note: Only two call sites recorded refusals; the render path did not. Every refusal is recorded now.

knownProductFindings.finding: A valid shaped subtitle line longer than 32 code points was rejected by native atlas staging.
knownProductFindings.note: The WebView and compositor model cells as whole shaped lines, but the staging validator still applied the deleted grapheme-cluster ceiling. It now mirrors MAX_CELL_CODE_POINTS per line and MAX_ATLAS_CODE_POINTS per page; the real 61-cue replay and a 34-code-point Rust boundary test pin the correction.

knownProductFindings.finding: Editing a cue sometimes does not commit: the edited text never appears.
knownProductFindings.note: The original occurrence was not reproducible after the sole WebView handle was explicitly selected. The durability claim is now separately proven by two application processes; active-window recovery is no longer conflated with relaunch coverage.

knownProductFindings.finding: Opening Render on a paused project could leave the native preview permanently idle until the customer seeked or played.
knownProductFindings.note: A paused element's only presentation can predate the armed requestVideoFrameCallback, and an occluded surface may never composite another frame; the load events only re-armed the callback and the no-clock draw guard returned bare, freezing the published state at idle. Load events on a settled paused element now run the same settled-snapshot publication as the seeked boundary, and the no-clock guard arms the bounded capture retry. Two component regressions pin both paths; the journey rerun against a rebuilt binary owns the end-to-end proof.

knownProductFindings.finding: A subtitle track authored before any video vanished from the editor the moment a video was opened.
knownProductFindings.note: The designed SRT-first preserve only recognized a null cache miss, but a freshly created media project scaffolds an EMPTY track, so hydration applied [] over the live rows; and nothing persisted the preserved rows into the new project, leaving even a surviving track one relaunch from loss. The hydrator now treats an empty scaffold inside the explicit SRT-first window like a miss, and the provenance seam persists the pending rows through the ordinary import path before claiming the badge. Proven end to end by the green srtOnlyMediaAttach run; manual media-free authoring without an uploaded document remains outside the carry-over and is recorded in that entry.

knownProductFindings.finding: A language-free (Format-mode) translated document proposed exactly the original track filename, so saving both as the same format collided and the second save produced nothing.
knownProductFindings.note: Translated documents without target languages now carry a _translated suffix; the naming rule moved into a pure tested util and the journey pins both proposed names.

knownProductFindings.finding: The continuity witness repeatedly reported a black frame immediately after playing backward seeks.
knownProductFindings.note: The recurring signature was the witness's own blind spot: a publication composed from a frozen source canvas captured BEFORE the witness attached is tainted and uninspectable, so its traced state naturally read black/no-video — the held-frame design at work, not a customer-visible flash. Such compositions now classify as unknown provenance inside the bounded unclassified window. The chase still produced two real product hardenings that remain: a playing seek boundary no longer snapshots the element (the transitioning decoder surface can legally read back black there), and the first captures of every seek generation reject a solid-black surface with one bounded readback.

knownProductFindings.finding: Rare application launches fail-fasted silently at startup (exit 0xC0000409) before the embedded WebDriver server became ready, before any log, data, or evidence file was written.
knownProductFindings.foundBy: editPersistRelaunch stress iteration 6/8 and the same scenario's seed-to-verify handoff, 2026-08-27
knownProductFindings.note: Both occurrences sat at the same seam: a relaunch phase opened the seed phase's reused WebView2 user-data folder while Edge's browser subprocesses were still releasing it asynchronously. The second occurrence proved the silence — backend stderr capture was armed and recorded nothing, ruling out a Rust panic and matching a WebView2 loader fail-fast on a busy profile. The two-process scenario runner now waits, bounded, for every WebView process still naming the profile to leave before launching the next phase. Environmental to profile-reusing test harnesses; a customer relaunching the installed application uses a profile whose previous owner exited seconds-to-minutes earlier, and no customer occurrence is known.

knownProductFindings.finding: Switching a playing project to a second file whose first frame is genuinely black left the main preview permanently blank over fully decoded media until the customer seeked or played.
knownProductFindings.note: loadeddata and canplay arrive in one task burst over the paused replacement source. Each runs the settled-capture boundary: the first's black-looking capture was skipped and armed a bounded retry, then the second bumped the capture generation without cancelling that pending retry. The stale handle blocked the new generation from arming its own retry while its callback exited on the generation mismatch without rescheduling, so no capture path remained for a paused element. The settled boundary now invalidates the pending retry exactly as the seek boundary always has; a component regression reproduces the burst and fails on the unfixed component, and the preserved journey screenshot shows the blank preview with the element at readyState 4.

knownProductFindings.finding: A successful media preparation could toast 'Processing failed: The active native media changed or is unavailable' when its own site-subtitle import was still persisting as generation started.
knownProductFindings.note: Resolving the active native media captured the local project revision and demanded the durable owner and every later local read match it exactly, so a same-project cue write landing mid-resolve read as a media change and failed the whole auto flow while the subtitles sat correctly on screen. Turbulence whose end state still names the captured project, asset and alias session AND whose revision genuinely advanced now retries a bounded full re-capture; an A-to-B switch, an A-to-B-to-A replacement (same revision restored), an undo (revision regressed), an alias remap and exhaustion all keep failing closed. Eleven resolver tests pin both directions. The four-window ASR break turned out to be a different root: see the zero-length tail segment finding.

knownProductFindings.finding: A windowed local transcription lost a whole window to 'Processing failed: The desktop host returned invalid ASR data' whenever the model's final word started at or past the window's decoded audio end.
knownProductFindings.foundBy: multiWindowAsrPersistence, named by its instrumented error-toast ledger
knownProductFindings.note: The host clamps a tail word's end to the decoded duration but permits its start to equal it, so a segment built from that word carried zero extent. The WebView boundary validator rightly refuses a payload holding a no-extent cue, the aggregate errored after the native job had already recorded success, and the visible rows reset to the empty baseline. The host now publishes only segments with extent; a Rust regression pins the exact offending payload (start 1000ms, end clamped to 1000ms) and fails without the fix.

media: pinned W3C Sintel trailer cached in managed external assets/e2e/source-switch-media

harnessLimitations.limitation: One run root per wdio invocation, not per spec.
harnessLimitations.consequence: Journeys are only independent when run one spec at a time. Several --spec flags in one invocation share a database, so the application restores the previous spec's project and the first-run controls never appear.
harnessLimitations.measured: unicodeCues and urlToPreview each pass alone and both fail together: '.url-field still not displayed' and 'the selected media never became playable'.
harnessLimitations.workedAround: package.json chains one invocation per spec.
harnessLimitations.properFix: A fresh root per spec. The root is created when the config loads because beforeSession is too late -- the service spawns the binary from the launcher, and assigning isolation later let a run read live user state while appearing isolated.

harnessLimitations.limitation: tauri-service active-window discovery is unavailable in some otherwise healthy embedded sessions.
harnessLimitations.consequence: Without an explicit handle, each element command can wait five seconds even though standard WebDriver is already attached to the rendered editor.
harnessLimitations.measured: Pinning the sole handle in the config removed the unavailable focus-discovery delay. Cross-process scenarios do not reuse or reload a WebDriver session.
harnessLimitations.workedAround: The harness performs a standard switchToWindow on the sole existing handle. It does not navigate, inject application state, mock IPC, or select a different product window.

suiteRun.how: guarded automation binary with one isolated profile and one desktop process per journey; persistence workflows additionally used separate seed and verification processes
suiteRun.result: real URL save, native decoded export, local ASR, narration plus aligned audio export, Gemini credential refusal, edited-cue persistence, Unicode persistence, translation persistence, and native tools green; full Rust workspace and 235 frontend files / 2179 assertions green
